problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-2x(t)-5y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=5x(t)-2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are $\lambda =-2\pm 5\text{i}.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.$\,$
Since 
{{field-1}},
the equilibrium point (origin) is {{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
Let $v=p+q\text{i},$ where $p,q\in {R}^{2},$ be an eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =a+b\text{i}.$

Then, a complex solution of the system is given by

$$
{x}_{\text{complex}}(t)=v{e}^{\lambda t}.
$$

Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{complex}}(t) & =v{e}^{(a+b\text{i})t} \\  & ={e}^{at}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt))(p+q\text{i}) \\  & ={e}^{at}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)p-\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)q)+\text{i}{e}^{at}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)p+\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)q).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\text{x}(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{at}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)p-\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)q)+{c}_{2}{e}^{at}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)p+\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)q),
$$

where the parts $(\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)p-\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)q)$ and $(\operatorname{sin}⁡(bt)p+\operatorname{cos}⁡(bt)q)$ are bounded.

Now, notice that $a=\text{Re}(\lambda )=-2<0$ and ${e}^{at}={e}^{-2t}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty .$ Thus, we have a spiral that is traversed toward the origin as $t\to \infty .$ 

Therefore, since $\text{Re}(\lambda )<0,$ the equilibrium point (origin) is $\text{a stable spiral (sink)}.$
